# Vertical overlay: Nuclear Reactors, Materials, and Waste

**Level:** CISA critical infrastructure sector (child of NAICS 22 Utilities)
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 221113 Nuclear Electric Power Generation. Nuclear electric generating station.
**Primary system:** Plant business network and work management system (non-safety)

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
SRMA: Department of Homeland Security (CISA); Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC); Department of Energy (DOE) - government-owned facilities

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**10 CFR 73.54 (with RG 5.71 Rev. 1 controls)**, 10 CFR 73.54. Binding, inspected (IP 71130.10) cyber rule for power reactors; RG 5.71 Rev. 1 supplies a NIST SP 800-53/800-82-derived control catalog suited to control-by-control gap analysis. Use 73.110/RG 5.96 for Part 53 plants.
Source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-10/section-73.54

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** Safeguards Information (SGI, 10 CFR 73.21-73.22); Cyber security plans and critical digital asset inventories; Export-controlled nuclear technology (10 CFR Part 810 / Part 110); CEII; Personnel access authorization data (10 CFR 73.56)
- **Critical systems:** Reactor protection and safety-related I&C; Plant process computers; Emergency preparedness communication systems; Security systems (PACS, alarm stations); Balance-of-plant DCS; Radiation monitoring systems
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** ; 
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** None noted
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Cyber attack on plant business network with attempted pivot to digital assets
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** Predictive maintenance for non-safety plant equipment

## Notes
Fuel cycle and materials licensees currently have no NRC cyber rule equivalent to 73.54 (not re-verified); CIRCIA would cover fuel cycle facilities once final.
